name: emw-pytme
help:
Wrapper for *pyTME* (Python Template Matching Engine), a GPU-accelerated template matching for cryo-EM and cryo-ET, developed by Valentin J. Maurer and Jan Kosinski at EMBL Hamburg.

Each tomogram is matched with *match_template* and its peaks are called with *postprocess* (RELION 5 and RELION 4 STAR files and pyTME orientations). The output particles have the same format as emw-pytom, with the pyTME score as rlnLCCmax.

The template and mask must have the voxel size of the tomograms (e.g. created with emw-pytom-create_template).

*Documentation*:
https://kosinskilab.github.io/pyTME/

*CITATION*:

Maurer, V. J., Siggel, M., & Kosinski, J. (2024). PyTME (Python Template Matching Engine): A fast, flexible, and multi-purpose template matching library for cryogenic electron microscopy data. SoftwareX, 25, 101636. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.softx.2024.101636

params.name: input_tomograms
params.label: Input tomograms (STAR):
params.help: STAR file with input tomograms

params.name: pytme.template
params.label: Template volume (MRC)
params.help: (-i/--template) Template at the voxel size of the tomograms, with the contrast of the tomograms (e.g. dark particles).

params.name: pytme.template-mask
params.label: Template mask (MRC)
params.help: (-I/--template-mask) Mask of the template, same box and voxel size. Optional: without a mask pyTME uses the whole template box.

params.name: pytme.invert-target-contrast
params.label: Invert tomogram contrast?
params.help: (--invert-target-contrast) Invert the tomogram contrast (multiply by -1). Usually not needed if the template has the contrast of the tomograms.

params.name: pytme.angular-sampling
params.label: Angular sampling (deg)
params.help: (-a/--angular-sampling) Angular sampling in degrees, lower values mean more rotations (10 ~ 7k, 5 ~ 53k rotations). If empty, it is derived from the particle diameter (--particle-diameter).

params.name: pytme.score
params.label: Score
params.help: (-s/--score) Scoring function. FLCSphericalMask is faster but assumes a spherical template mask, use FLC for other masks.

params.name: pytme.background-correction
params.label: Phase-scrambling background?
params.help: (--background-correction phase-scrambling) Transform the scores into SNR-like values using a phase-scrambled template as background (similar to the random phase correction of PyTom).

params.name: pytme.extra_args
params.label: match_template extra arguments
params.help:
Extra command-line arguments to pass directly to match_template (pyTME 0.3.3), exactly as they would be typed on the command line (e.g. "--target-mask mask.mrc --no-filter-target"). Options not exposed above include:
--target-mask (skip regions outside this mask)
--wedge-axes (projection and tilt axes, default 2,0)
--no-filter-target (do not filter the tomogram)
--no-pass-smooth (hard edge band-pass)
--phase-shift (phase plate phase shift, in degrees)
--centering / --pad-edges / --interpolation-order / --use-memmap
--memory-scaling (fraction of memory to use, default 0.85)
--no-use-optimized-set (random uniform rotations)
See the pyTME documentation for the full list: https://kosinskilab.github.io/pyTME/

Options already set above (or computed automatically from the acquisition/batch data, such as --target, --tilt-angles or --defocus) must not be repeated here -- doing so will fail the job with an error. Single-letter options (-m, -i, -a, ...) are not recognized here, use their long form.

params.name: pytme.lowpass
params.label: Low-pass
params.help: (--lowpass) Resolution (A) to low-pass filter the template and tomogram. Leave empty to not low-pass filter.

params.name: pytme.highpass
params.label: High-pass
params.help: (--highpass) Resolution (A) to high-pass filter the template and tomogram. Leave empty to not high-pass filter.

params.name: pytme.whiten-spectrum
params.label: Spectral whitening?
params.help: (--whiten-spectrum) Apply spectral whitening to the template and tomogram.

params.name: pytme.tilt-weighting
params.label: Tilt weighting
params.help: (--tilt-weighting) Weighting of the individual tilts of the wedge. The tilt angles and accumulated dose (--tilt-angles) are taken from the tilt series STAR files; relion and grigorieff use the dose, angle uses a cosine weighting and none a binary wedge.

params.name: pytme.ctf
params.label: CTF model
params.help: CTF of the template, from the tilt series STAR files defocus (rlnDefocusU/V/Angle): the mean defocus of all the tilts (--defocus) or the defocus of each tilt (--ctf-file). pyTME 0.3.3 does not use the astigmatism in either case (mean of defocus U and V). Voltage, spherical aberration and amplitude contrast come from the acquisition.

params.name: pytme.flip-phase
params.label: Phase-flip the CTF?
params.help: Phase-flipping CTF correction of the template (as for phase-flipped tomograms), otherwise --no-flip-phase.

params.name: pytme_postprocess.particle-diameter
params.label: Particle diameter (A)
params.help: Particle diameter (A). Used for the default minimum distance between peaks (its radius, as PyTom) and to derive the angular sampling (--particle-diameter) if it is not given.

params.name: pytme_postprocess.num-peaks
params.label: Maximum number of particles
params.help: (--num-peaks) Upper limit of peaks to call per tomogram.

params.name: pytme_postprocess.min-distance
params.label: Between peaks
params.help: (--min-distance) Minimum distance (A) between peaks, converted to voxels of the tomograms. By default, the particle radius.

params.name: pytme_postprocess.min-boundary-distance
params.label: To edges
params.help: (--min-boundary-distance) Minimum distance (A) of peaks to the tomogram edges, converted to voxels. Leave empty for no minimum distance (see Mask edges).

params.name: pytme_postprocess.mask-edges
params.label: Mask edges?
params.help: (--mask-edges) Do not call peaks from scores computed from padded densities: if no distance to the edges is given, half of the template box is used.

params.name: pytme_postprocess.min-score
params.label: Minimum score
params.help: (--min-score) Minimum score of the peaks. Leave empty to use only the false positives cutoff (the score scale depends on the data, template and filters).

params.name: pytme_postprocess.n-false-positives
params.label: False positives
params.help: (--n-false-positives) Number of accepted false positives to determine the minimum score from the score statistics (Rickgauer et al. 2017). The largest of this and the minimum score is used. Leave both empty to keep the maximum number of particles.

params.name: pytme_postprocess.peak-caller
params.label: Peak caller
params.help: (--peak-caller) Peak caller for local maxima identification.

params.name: gpus
params.label: GPUs
params.help: If it is a single number (N), N threads with one GPU each (0..N-1). Several values are specific GPU IDs, one thread each, and comma separated values are the GPUs of one thread, e.g. "0,1 2,3" (pyTME splits the rotations among them). Each thread picks one tomogram at a time. If empty, pyTME runs on CPU.

params.name: pytme.cores
params.label: CPU cores
params.help: (-n) Number of CPU cores used without GPUs.

params.label: Launchers
params.help: Launchers to use for the different programs

params.name: launcher
params.label: pyTME
params.help: Launcher to use for the pyTME programs (match_template and postprocess). Leave empty to use EMWRAP_CONFIG default.
